The record stays material-pending; no accepted, scalar or Korean name or product application is assigned.

This is neither completed representative identity nor completed name-scope hold. The two new502 pauses are source-access details, not additional primary pending counts.

records.region: Northern Ontario, Canada; Aquatuk–Sutton river setting and the Hudson Bay coast near Little Cape.
records.candidate_name_role: Directly supported middle river component only. Sutton River is a distinct supported lower receiving component. No completed whole-system identity is asserted.
records.material_pending_reason: No usable original establishes the complete selected southern opening and upper/western corridor, including any lake, pond or wetland through-links before the directly mapped Aquatuk segment. The report supports regional Aquatuk–Sutton connectivity but does not resolve all selected intervening western passages. These are material geographic gaps, not merely unnamed reaches.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The source-supported route contains a distinct Aquatuk River component followed downstream by lower Sutton River. It is separate from the neighboring Kinushseo River. The coastal original shows the Sutton channel widening and dividing into its estuarine/intertidal fan near Little Cape and Hudson Bay. The model endpoint lies in that coastal transition, rather than being proof of an exact surveyed river mouth or open-water shoreline. Hawley Lake is independently identified as the source of Sutton River, but that does not put Hawley Lake on this selected Aquatuk approach. Aquatuk Lake is a distinct study water; proximity and a generalized line do not establish the selection’s lake entry, exit or complete headward route.
records.completion_scope: The source-supported route contains a distinct Aquatuk River component followed downstream by lower Sutton River. It is separate from the neighboring Kinushseo River. The coastal original shows the Sutton channel widening and dividing into its estuarine/intertidal fan near Little Cape and Hudson Bay. The model endpoint lies in that coastal transition, rather than being proof of an exact surveyed river mouth or open-water shoreline. Hawley Lake is independently identified as the source of Sutton River, but that does not put Hawley Lake on this selected Aquatuk approach. Aquatuk Lake is a distinct study water; proximity and a generalized line do not establish the selection’s lake entry, exit or complete headward route. No usable original establishes the complete selected southern opening and upper/western corridor, including any lake, pond or wetland through-links before the directly mapped Aquatuk segment. The report supports regional Aquatuk–Sutton connectivity but does not resolve all selected intervening western passages. These are material geographic gaps, not merely unnamed reaches.
records.supported_name_scope: The eastern middle corridor is labelled Aquatuk River on the original thematic map; the downstream lower corridor is labelled Sutton River on the coastal original. The field-study report independently distinguishes both rivers and shows their regional connection. Neither name is assigned to the unresolved selected southern opening, every upper passage, or any nearby lake.

component_scope_limits: The complete selected opening and upper/western through-route remain unestablished; whole-system naming is therefore incomplete.
The source identities Aquatuk River and Sutton River apply to distinct supported components, not to every feeder, lake or the entire selected model.
The field report supports their regional junction, but its generalized figure and malformed Aquatuk coordinate are insufficient for all intervening selected passages.
Neither a precise modern distributary alignment nor the exact tidal/shoreline position is established by historical thematic maps.
Shared or modified base hydrography is not proof of independent underlying hydrographic observations.
No current formal registry decision, Indigenous-name equivalence, Korean name, surveyed length or present hydraulic condition is established.

records.region: Nunavik, Québec, Canada; Rivière False corridor east of Kuujjuaq and the Kohlmeister-side marine-estuarine setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Rivière False is supported for the regional named corridor and lower estuarine approach. Its representative identity for the entire selected group remains unestablished because the southeastern opening and intermediate lake/river through-links lack adequate original source correspondence.
records.material_pending_reason: The southeastern opening, successive upper lake and stream passages, western bend, middle lake connections and uncovered lower interior joins remain unestablished. The separately supported False River estuarine approach does not close those upstream gaps.
records.geographic_disambiguation: CEHQ’s original regional map labels Rivière False along the northward interior corridor. RG2013-04-C001 distinguishes its Kohlmeister-side terminal setting east of Kuujjuaq from the Koksoak waterway. The independent Falconbridge GM62436 field-assessment report shows the lower False River entering a marine estuary on its annotated Landsat image and describes that outlet in the accompanying prose. This supports the lower river candidate and terminal approach, but not every selected opening, lake connection or intermediate join. The whole group remains source-material-pending.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
